Shell Programming with Bash and vi/vim

What is a Shell?

Definition: Command-line interpreter for OS services

Common Shells:

  • Bash - Most common on Linux
  • Zsh - Extended features
  • Fish - User-friendly

Shell Script: Text file with shell commands

Primary Uses:

  • Automating repetitive tasks
  • Gluing programs together
  • System administration
  • Data processing pipelines

Why learn vi/vim?

  • Available on every Unix/Linux system
  • Script editing without leaving terminal
  • Fast navigation and manipulation

Your First Shell Script

Step 1: Create file with vi

vi first_script.sh

Step 2: Enter insert mode (i) and type:

#!/bin/bash
# Author: Kedir Jemal
echo "Welcome to shell programming"
echo "Current date: $(date)"
echo "Directory: $(pwd)"

Step 3: Save and exit (Esc then :wq)

Step 4: Make executable

chmod +x first_script.sh

Step 5: Run

./first_script.sh

Shebang #!/bin/bash specifies interpreter

Conditional Statements

Syntax:

if [ condition ]; then
    commands
elif [ other ]; then
    commands
else
    commands
fi

Examples:

if [[ "$name" == "Hundessa" ]]; then
    echo "Welcome"
fi

age=25
if [[ $age -ge 18 ]]; then
    echo "Adult"
else
    echo "Minor"
fi

score=85
if [[ $score -ge 90 ]]; then
    echo "A"
elif [[ $score -ge 80 ]]; then
    echo "B"
else
    echo "C"
fi

Logical Operators

Combining conditions:

# AND - both true
if [[ $age -ge 18 && "$license" == "yes" ]]; then
    echo "Can drive"
fi

# OR - at least one true
if [[ "$day" == "Sat" || "$day" == "Sun" ]]; then
    echo "Weekend"
fi

# NOT - negate
if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
    echo "File missing"
fi

Command chaining:

# Execute second only if first succeeds
mkdir newdir && cd newdir

# Execute second only if first fails
cd /nonexistent || echo "Failed"

Old style (-a and -o):

    echo "Can drive"
fi

C-style for:

for ((i=1; i<=5; i++)); do

Break and continue:

While and Until Loops

While loop:

counter=1
while [[ $counter -le 10 ]]; do
    echo "Counter: $counter"
    ((counter++))
done

Read file line by line:

while IFS=: read -r user uid; do
    echo "User: $user, UID: $uid"
done < /etc/passwd

Infinite loop with break:

count=0
while true; do
    ((count++))
    if [[ $count -ge 5 ]]; then
        break
    fi
done

Until loop (opposite of while):

counter=1
until [[ $counter -gt 10 ]]; do
    echo "$counter"
    ((counter++))
done

Wait for file:

while [[ ! -f "data.txt" ]]; do
    sleep 2
done

Command Line Arguments

Basic parsing:

#!/bin/bash
echo "Script: $0"
echo "First arg: $1"
echo "All args: $@"
echo "Arg count: $#"

Using getopts:

while getopts "f:n:vh" opt; do
    case $opt in
        f)
            file="$OPTARG"
            ;;
        n)
            name="$OPTARG"
            ;;
        v)
            verbose=1
            ;;
        h)
            show_help
            ;;
    esac
done
shift $((OPTIND-1))

Manual parsing:

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case $1 in
        --mode)
            mode="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        --help)
            exit 0
            ;;
        *)
            input="$1"
            shift
            ;;
    esac
done

Why Shell Scripting for SysAdmins and HPC?

System Administration Uses: - User account management (create, modify, delete) - Log rotation and analysis - Backup automation - System monitoring and alerting - Software deployment across multiple nodes - Security audit scripts - Configuration management

HPC Specific Uses: - Job submission and management - Workflow automation - Data staging (input/output) - Job dependency handling - Cluster health monitoring - Resource usage reporting - Parallel job coordination

Example Ethiopian HPC Context: - Ethiopian universities and research centers - Weather modeling at Ethiopian Meteorology Institute - Genomics research at Ethiopian Biotechnology Institute - Climate modeling for agriculture planning

What is a Job Scheduler?

Definition: A job scheduler is software that manages batch jobs in a multi-user HPC environment.

Why Schedulers are Needed: - Fair resource allocation among users - Maximize cluster utilization - Queue management - Job dependency handling - Resource reservation

Common HPC Schedulers: | Scheduler | Description | |———–|————-| | Slurm | Most common on modern clusters | | Torque/PBS | Legacy but still widely used | | LSF | IBM platform | | SGE | Sun Grid Engine |

This Lesson Covers: - Torque (PBS) commands and scripting - Slurm commands and scripting - Integration with Bash

Torque/PBS Basics

Torque Components: | Component | Purpose | |———–|———| | pbs_server | Central management daemon | | pbs_sched | Scheduler daemon | | pbs_mom | Node execution daemon |

Basic Torque Commands: | Command | Purpose | |———|———| | qsub | Submit a job | | qstat | View job status | | qdel | Delete a job | | qhold | Hold a job | | qrls | Release a held job | | qalter | Modify job attributes | | pbsnodes | View node status |

Common qstat Options:

qstat              # Show user's jobs
qstat -a           # Show all jobs
qstat -n           # Show node allocation
qstat -f jobid     # Full job details
qstat -q           # Show queues

Torque/PBS Job Script Structure

Basic PBS Job Script:

#!/bin/bash
#PBS -N my_job           # Job name
#PBS -l nodes=2:ppn=4    # 2 nodes, 4 cores per node
#PBS -l walltime=01:00:00 # Max runtime
#PBS -q batch            # Queue name
#PBS -j oe               # Join output/error
#PBS -o /path/to/output  # Output file
#PBS -e /path/to/error   # Error file
#PBS -M user@domain.com  # Email address
#PBS -m abe              # Email on abort, begin, end

cd $PBS_O_WORKDIR        # Change to submission dir
echo "Job started on $(date)"
echo "Running on node: $(hostname)"

# Your actual work here
./my_program

echo "Job finished on $(date)"

Explanation of PBS Directives:

  • #PBS lines are interpreted by qsub, not bash
  • $PBS_O_WORKDIR - Original working directory
  • $PBS_NODEFILE - File with allocated node list
  • $PBS_JOBID - Unique job identifier

Torque/PBS Advanced Script

Complete PBS Script with Error Handling:

#!/bin/bash
#PBS -N hpc_simulation
#PBS -l nodes=4:ppn=8
#PBS -l walltime=12:00:00
#PBS -l mem=32gb
#PBS -q research
#PBS -j oe
#PBS -M mesfindiro@gmail.com
#PBS -m ae

set -euo pipefail

# Change to submission directory
cd $PBS_O_WORKDIR || { echo "CD failed"; exit 1; }

# Create job-specific temp directory
TEMP_DIR="/scratch/${PBS_JOBID}"
mkdir -p "$TEMP_DIR"

# Copy input data to scratch
echo "Staging input data..."
cp input_data/* "$TEMP_DIR/"

# Run MPI application
mpirun -np 32 -machinefile $PBS_NODEFILE ./simulation

# Copy results back
echo "Staging output data..."
cp "$TEMP_DIR"/results_* output/

# Cleanup
rm -rf "$TEMP_DIR"

echo "Job $PBS_JOBID completed on $(date)"

Key PBS Variables:

Variable Description
$PBS_O_WORKDIR Submission directory
$PBS_JOBID Job ID
$PBS_NODEFILE List of allocated nodes
$PBS_QUEUE Queue name
$PBS_NODENUM Number of nodes

Torque/PBS Job Management Scripts

Submit Array Job:

#!/bin/bash
#PBS -t 1-100            # Array of 100 tasks
#PBS -l nodes=1:ppn=1    # 1 core per task

cd $PBS_O_WORKDIR

# Use array index to process different inputs
INPUT_FILE="input_${PBS_ARRAYID}.txt"
OUTPUT_FILE="output_${PBS_ARRAYID}.txt"

./process_data "$INPUT_FILE" "$OUTPUT_FILE"

Monitor Jobs Script:

#!/bin/bash
# monitor_pbs.sh - Check job status

USER="hundessa"

echo "=== Job Status for $USER ==="
qstat -u "$USER" | while read line; do
    echo "$line"
done

echo ""
echo "=== Running Jobs ==="
qstat -u "$USER" | grep " R "

echo ""
echo "=== Queued Jobs ==="
qstat -u "$USER" | grep " Q "

echo ""
echo "=== Node Status ==="
pbsnodes -a | grep -E "state|name"

Delete All Jobs Script:

#!/bin/bash
# delete_all_jobs.sh

read -p "Delete all your jobs? (y/n): " confirm

if [[ "$confirm" == "y" ]]; then
    for job in $(qstat -u "$USER" | awk 'NR>2 {print $1}'); do
        echo "Deleting job: $job"
        qdel "$job"
    done
    echo "All jobs deleted"
fi

## Slurm Job Script Structure

**Basic Slurm Job Script:**

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=my_job
#SBATCH --nodes=2
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=4
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH --time=01:00:00
#SBATCH --partition=batch
#SBATCH --output=%j.out
#SBATCH --error=%j.err
#SBATCH --mail-user=almaz@ethioresearch.et
#SBATCH --mail-type=ALL

# %j expands to job ID

echo "Job started on $(date)"
echo "Running on node: $(hostname)"
echo "Job ID: $SLURM_JOB_ID"
echo "Node list: $SLURM_JOB_NODELIST"

# Your work
srun ./my_program

echo "Job finished on $(date)"

Slurm vs Torque Comparison: | Torque/PBS | Slurm | Description | |————|——-|————-| | #PBS -l nodes=N | #SBATCH --nodes=N | Node count | | #PBS -l walltime=T | #SBATCH --time=T | Time limit | | #PBS -N name | #SBATCH --job-name=name | Job name | | qsub | sbatch | Submit | | qstat | squeue | Status | | qdel | scancel | Delete |

Slurm Advanced Script

Complete Slurm Script with Resource Request:

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=hpc_weather
#SBATCH --nodes=4
#SBATCH --ntasks=32
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=2
#SBATCH --mem=64G
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00
#SBATCH --partition=gpu
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:4
#SBATCH --output=logs/%j.out
#SBATCH --error=logs/%j.err
#SBATCH --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL
#SBATCH --mail-user=chaltu@climate.et

set -euo pipefail

# Load required modules
module purge
module load gcc/10.2
module load openmpi/4.1
module load cuda/11.2

# Change to submission directory
cd $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR

# Create unique scratch directory
SCRATCH="/scratch/${SLURM_JOB_ID}"
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH"

# Stage input data
rsync -av input/ "$SCRATCH/"

# Run the application
cd "$SCRATCH"
srun ./weather_model parameters.dat

# Stage output back
rsync -av results/ "$SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR/results/"

# Cleanup
cd /
rm -rf "$SCRATCH"

echo "Job $SLURM_JOB_ID completed"

Important Slurm Variables: | Variable | Description | |———-|————-| | $SLURM_JOB_ID | Job ID | | $SLURM_JOB_NAME | Job name | | $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR | Submission directory | | $SLURM_JOB_NODELIST | Allocated nodes | | $SLURM_NTASKS | Total tasks | | $SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK | CPUs per task |

Slurm Job Arrays

System Administration - User Management

Create Multiple Users Script:

#!/bin/bash
# create_users.sh - Batch user creation for HPC cluster

USER_LIST="users.txt"
DEFAULT_GROUP="hpcusers"
HOME_BASE="/home"

if [[ ! -f "$USER_LIST" ]]; then
    echo "Error: $USER_LIST not found"
    echo "Format: username:fullname:project"
    exit 1
fi

while IFS=: read -r username fullname project; do
    echo "Creating user: $username"
    
    # Create user with home directory
    useradd -m -d "$HOME_BASE/$username" -s /bin/bash -c "$fullname" "$username"
    
    # Add to HPC group
    usermod -aG "$DEFAULT_GROUP" "$username"
    
    # Set default password (force change on first login)
    echo "$username:TempPass123" | chpasswd
    chage -d 0 "$username"
    
    # Create project directory
    mkdir -p "/project/$project/$username"
    chown "$username:$DEFAULT_GROUP" "/project/$project/$username"
    
    # Set quota (if enabled)
    # setquota -u "$username" 10G 20G 0 0 /home
    
    echo "Created: $username - $fullname"
done < "$USER_LIST"

echo "User creation completed"

Modify User Quota Script:

#!/bin/bash
# set_quota.sh - Set HPC storage quotas

USERNAME="$1"
SOFT_LIMIT="${2:-10G}"
HARD_LIMIT="${3:-20G}"

if [[ -z "$USERNAME" ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <username> [soft_limit] [hard_limit]"
    echo "Example: $0 bontu 50G 100G"
    exit 1
fi

# Set quota on /home partition
setquota -u "$USERNAME" "$SOFT_LIMIT" "$HARD_LIMIT" 0 0 /home

# Set quota on /scratch partition
setquota -u "$USERNAME" "$SOFT_LIMIT" "$HARD_LIMIT" 0 0 /scratch

echo "Quota set for $USERNAME: soft=$SOFT_LIMIT hard=$HARD_LIMIT"

# Report current usage
repquota -u /home | grep "$USERNAME"

System Administration - Log Management

Log Rotation Script:

#!/bin/bash
# rotate_logs.sh - Rotate and compress HPC logs

LOG_DIR="/var/log/hpc"
ARCHIVE_DIR="/archive/logs"
RETENTION_DAYS=90

# Create archive directory if not exists
mkdir -p "$ARCHIVE_DIR"

# Rotate slurm logs
if [[ -d "$LOG_DIR/slurm" ]]; then
    cd "$LOG_DIR/slurm"
    for log in slurm*.log; do
        if [[ -f "$log" ]]; then
            # Get date from log or use modification time
            date_str=$(stat -c %y "$log" | cut -d' ' -f1)
            tar -czf "$ARCHIVE_DIR/slurm_${date_str}.tar.gz" "$log"
            rm "$log"
            echo "Rotated: $log"
        fi
    done
fi

# Rotate torque logs
if [[ -d "$LOG_DIR/torque" ]]; then
    cd "$LOG_DIR/torque"
    for log in *.log.*; do
        if [[ -f "$log" ]]; then
            gzip "$log"
            mv "$log.gz" "$ARCHIVE_DIR/"
            echo "Compressed: $log"
        fi
    done
fi

# Remove old archives
find "$ARCHIVE_DIR" -type f -mtime +$RETENTION_DAYS -delete

echo "Log rotation completed at $(date)"

Log Analysis for Job Failures:

#!/bin/bash
# analyze_failures.sh - Find common job failure reasons

LOG_DIR="/var/log/slurm"
OUTPUT_FILE="failure_report_$(date +%Y%m%d).txt"

echo "=== Job Failure Analysis Report ===" > "$OUTPUT_FILE"
echo "Generated: $(date)" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
echo "" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"

# Count failures by exit code
echo "Failures by exit code:" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
grep -h "exit code" "$LOG_DIR"/*.out 2>/dev/null | \
    awk '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"

echo "" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"

# Count failures by node
echo "Failures by node:" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
grep -h "Node" "$LOG_DIR"/*.err 2>/dev/null | \
    awk '{print $3}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"

echo "" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"

# Top error messages
echo "Top error messages:" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
grep -h -i "error\|failed\|timeout" "$LOG_DIR"/*.err 2>/dev/null | \
    sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20 >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"

echo "Report saved to: $OUTPUT_FILE"

Cluster Health Check Script:

#!/bin/bash
# health_check.sh - Comprehensive HPC cluster health check

ALERT_EMAIL="sysadmin@ethioresearch.et"
REPORT_FILE="/tmp/cluster_health_$(date +%Y%m%d).txt"

{
    echo "=== HPC Cluster Health Report ==="
    echo "Date: $(date)"
    echo "Hostname: $(hostname)"
    echo ""
    
    # Check load average
    echo "=== System Load ==="
    uptime
    echo ""
    
    # Check memory
    echo "=== Memory Usage ==="
    free -h
    echo ""
    
    # Check disk space on critical partitions
    echo "=== Disk Usage ==="
    df -h /home /scratch /project /var
    echo ""
    
    # Check Slurm controller status
    echo "=== Slurm Controller ==="
    systemctl status slurmctld --no-pager | grep "Active"
    echo ""
    
    # Check number of down nodes
    echo "=== Node Status ==="
    DOWN_NODES=$(sinfo -o "%t" | grep -c "down\|drain")
    TOTAL_NODES=$(sinfo -o "%t" | wc -l)
    echo "Total nodes: $TOTAL_NODES"
    echo "Down/Drained nodes: $DOWN_NODES"
    echo ""
    
    # Check pending jobs
    PENDING=$(squeue -t PD -h | wc -l)
    RUNNING=$(squeue -t R -h | wc -l)
    echo "=== Job Queue ==="
    echo "Pending jobs: $PENDING"
    echo "Running jobs: $RUNNING"
    echo ""
    
    # Check license usage (if applicable)
    echo "=== License Usage ==="
    # lmstat -a -c /path/to/license.dat | grep "Users of"
    
} > "$REPORT_FILE"

# Send alert if issues found
if [[ $DOWN_NODES -gt 0 ]] || [[ $PENDING -gt 100 ]]; then
    mail -s "HPC Cluster Alert" "$ALERT_EMAIL" < "$REPORT_FILE"
fi

# Print summary
cat "$REPORT_FILE"

HPC Workflow Automation

Complete Analysis Pipeline Script:

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=genomics_pipeline
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=8
#SBATCH --mem=32G
#SBATCH --time=48:00:00
#SBATCH --partition=batch
#SBATCH --array=1-50
#SBATCH --output=logs/pipeline_%A_%a.out

# Genomics data processing pipeline for Ethiopian research
# Author: Jiru Demisse - Ethiopian Biotechnology Institute

set -euo pipefail

# Configuration
DATA_DIR="/data/genomics"
REFERENCE="/ref/ethiopian_reference.fa"
OUTPUT_BASE="/results/$(date +%Y%m%d)"
SAMPLE_LIST="samples.txt"

# Get sample name for this array task
SAMPLE=$(sed -n "${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}p" "$SAMPLE_LIST")
SAMPLE_OUTPUT="${OUTPUT_BASE}/${SAMPLE}"

# Create output directory
mkdir -p "$SAMPLE_OUTPUT"

echo "Processing sample: $SAMPLE"
echo "Start time: $(date)"

# Step 1: Quality control
echo "Step 1: Quality Control"
fastqc "${DATA_DIR}/${SAMPLE}.fastq" -o "$SAMPLE_OUTPUT/"

# Step 2: Trimming
echo "Step 2: Trimming adapters"
trimmomatic SE "${DATA_DIR}/${SAMPLE}.fastq" \
    "$SAMPLE_OUTPUT/${SAMPLE}_trimmed.fastq" \
    ILLUMINACLIP:adapters.fa:2:30:10 \
    LEADING:3 TRAILING:3 SLIDINGWINDOW:4:15 MINLEN:36

# Step 3: Alignment
echo "Step 3: Alignment to reference"
bwa mem -t 8 "$REFERENCE" \
    "$SAMPLE_OUTPUT/${SAMPLE}_trimmed.fastq" > \
    "$SAMPLE_OUTPUT/${SAMPLE}.sam"

# Step 4: Convert to BAM and sort
echo "Step 4: BAM conversion"
samtools view -bS "$SAMPLE_OUTPUT/${SAMPLE}.sam" | \
    samtools sort -o "$SAMPLE_OUTPUT/${SAMPLE}.bam"

# Step 5: Index BAM
echo "Step 5: Indexing"
samtools index "$SAMPLE_OUTPUT/${SAMPLE}.bam"

# Step 6: Variant calling
echo "Step 6: Variant calling"
bcftools mpileup -f "$REFERENCE" "$SAMPLE_OUTPUT/${SAMPLE}.bam" | \
    bcftools call -mv -o "$SAMPLE_OUTPUT/${SAMPLE}.vcf"

# Step 7: Cleanup intermediate files
rm "$SAMPLE_OUTPUT/${SAMPLE}.sam"
rm "$SAMPLE_OUTPUT/${SAMPLE}_trimmed.fastq"

echo "End time: $(date)"
echo "Pipeline completed for sample: $SAMPLE"

Job Dependency Management

Slurm Job Dependencies:

#!/bin/bash
# submit_workflow.sh - Submit jobs with dependencies

# Submit preprocessing job
PREPROC_JOB=$(sbatch --parsable preprocess.slurm)
echo "Preprocessing job: $PREPROC_JOB"

# Submit analysis job (runs after preprocessing)
ANALYSIS_JOB=$(sbatch --parsable --dependency=afterok:$PREPROC_JOB analysis.slurm)
echo "Analysis job: $ANALYSIS_JOB"

# Submit postprocessing (runs after analysis)
POSTPROC_JOB=$(sbatch --parsable --dependency=afterok:$ANALYSIS_JOB postprocess.slurm)
echo "Postprocessing job: $POSTPROC_JOB"

# Submit cleanup (runs after any job, even if fails)
CLEANUP_JOB=$(sbatch --parsable --dependency=afterany:$POSTPROC_JOB cleanup.slurm)

echo "Workflow submitted successfully"

Dependency Types in Slurm: | Dependency | Meaning | |————|———| | after:jobid | Start after job starts | | afterok:jobid | Start after job succeeds | | afternotok:jobid | Start after job fails | | afterany:jobid | Start after job completes (any status) | | before:jobid | Start before specified job |

Torque Job Dependencies:

#!/bin/bash
# PBS dependency example

# Submit first job
JOB1=$(qsub job1.pbs)

# Submit second job (depends on first)
qsub -W depend=afterok:$JOB1 job2.pbs

# Submit job that depends on multiple
qsub -W depend=afterok:${JOB1}:${JOB2} job3.pbs

# Job that starts after any completion
qsub -W depend=afterany:$JOB1 job4.pbs

#!/bin/bash
# user_usage.sh - Report resource usage for a user

USERNAME="$1"
DAYS="${2:-7}"

if [[ -z "$USERNAME" ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <username> [days]"
    exit 1
fi

echo "=== Resource Usage Report for $USERNAME ==="
echo "Period: Last $DAYS days"
echo ""

# Slurm accounting
echo "Slurm Jobs:"
sacct -u "$USERNAME" -S "now-${DAYS}days" \
    --format=JobID,JobName,Partition,ReqNodes,ReqMem,State,Elapsed,ExitCode \
    --noheader | head -50

echo ""
echo "Summary:"
sacct -u "$USERNAME" -S "now-${DAYS}days" \
    --format=ReqNodes,ReqMem,State --noheader | \
    awk '
    /COMPLETED/ {completed++; total_nodes+=$1}
    /FAILED/ {failed++}
    /CANCELLED/ {cancelled++}
    END {
        print "Completed jobs: " completed
        print "Failed jobs: " failed
        print "Cancelled jobs: " cancelled
        print "Total node requests: " total_nodes
    }'

echo ""
echo "Storage Usage:"
quota -u "$USERNAME" 2>/dev/null || echo "Quota command not available"

echo ""
echo "Processes Running:"
ps -u "$USERNAME" --no-headers | wc -l

Automated Job Submission Scripts

Parameter Sweep Script:

#!/bin/bash
# param_sweep.sh - Submit multiple jobs with varying parameters

PARAM_FILE="parameters.txt"
TEMPLATE="template.slurm"

if [[ ! -f "$PARAM_FILE" ]] || [[ ! -f "$TEMPLATE" ]]; then
    echo "Error: parameters.txt or template.slurm missing"
    exit 1
fi

JOB_IDS=()

while IFS= read -r params; do
    # Skip comments and empty lines
    [[ "$params" =~ ^#.*$ ]] && continue
    [[ -z "$params" ]] && continue
    
    # Create job-specific script
    JOB_SCRIPT="job_${RANDOM}.slurm"
    cp "$TEMPLATE" "$JOB_SCRIPT"
    
    # Replace placeholders
    sed -i "s/__PARAMS__/$params/g" "$JOB_SCRIPT"
    
    # Submit job
    JOB_ID=$(sbatch --parsable "$JOB_SCRIPT")
    JOB_IDS+=("$JOB_ID")
    
    echo "Submitted job $JOB_ID with parameters: $params"
    
    # Cleanup
    # rm "$JOB_SCRIPT"
    
done < "$PARAM_FILE"

echo ""
echo "Submitted ${#JOB_IDS[@]} jobs"
echo "Job IDs: ${JOB_IDS[@]}"

Checkpoint-Restart Script:

#!/bin/bash
# checkpoint_job.sh - Job with checkpoint/restart capability

CHECKPOINT_DIR="/scratch/${SLURM_JOB_ID}/checkpoints"
CHECKPOINT_FILE="$CHECKPOINT_DIR/state.chk"
MAX_RUNTIME=3600  # 1 hour per segment

mkdir -p "$CHECKPOINT_DIR"

# Function to save checkpoint
save_checkpoint() {
    echo "Saving checkpoint at $(date)"
    # Save application state
    kill -USR1 $APP_PID
    wait $APP_PID
    touch "$CHECKPOINT_FILE"
}

# Function to restore from checkpoint
restore_checkpoint() {
    if [[ -f "$CHECKPOINT_FILE" ]]; then
        echo "Restoring from checkpoint at $(date)"
        # Resume application from checkpoint
        ./app --restore "$CHECKPOINT_DIR"
    else
        echo "Starting fresh at $(date)"
        ./app &
    fi
}

# Set trap for time limit
SECONDS=0
while true; do
    restore_checkpoint
    APP_PID=$!
    
    # Wait for time limit or completion
    sleep $MAX_RUNTIME
    
    if kill -0 $APP_PID 2>/dev/null; then
        save_checkpoint
    else
        break
    fi
done

echo "Job completed at $(date)"

Data Transfer and Staging Scripts

Parallel Data Transfer Script:

#!/bin/bash
# parallel_transfer.sh - Transfer large datasets in parallel

SOURCE_DIR="$1"
DEST_DIR="$2"
PARALLEL_JOBS="${3:-4}"

if [[ -z "$SOURCE_DIR" ]] || [[ -z "$DEST_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <source_dir> <dest_dir> [parallel_jobs]"
    exit 1
fi

# Create destination
mkdir -p "$DEST_DIR"

# Transfer function
transfer_file() {
    local file="$1"
    local dest="$2"
    echo "Transferring: $file"
    rsync -av --progress "$file" "$dest"
}

export -f transfer_file

# Find all files and transfer in parallel
find "$SOURCE_DIR" -type f -name "*.fastq" | \
    xargs -P "$PARALLEL_JOBS" -I {} bash -c 'transfer_file "$@"' _ {} "$DEST_DIR"

echo "Transfer completed"

Staging Script for Batch Jobs:

#!/bin/bash
# stage_data.sh - Stage input data for HPC job

JOB_ID="$1"
INPUT_MANIFEST="$2"
STAGE_DIR="/scratch/stage/${JOB_ID}"

if [[ -z "$JOB_ID" ]] || [[ -z "$INPUT_MANIFEST" ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <job_id> <input_manifest>"
    exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$STAGE_DIR"

echo "Staging data for job $JOB_ID"

while IFS= read -r line; do
    # Format: source_path,destination_name
    SOURCE=$(echo "$line" | cut -d',' -f1)
    DEST=$(echo "$line" | cut -d',' -f2)
    
    if [[ -f "$SOURCE" ]]; then
        cp "$SOURCE" "$STAGE_DIR/$DEST"
        echo "Staged: $SOURCE -> $STAGE_DIR/$DEST"
    elif [[ -d "$SOURCE" ]]; then
        cp -r "$SOURCE" "$STAGE_DIR/$DEST"
        echo "Staged directory: $SOURCE"
    else
        echo "Warning: $SOURCE not found" >&2
    fi
done < "$INPUT_MANIFEST"

echo "Staging complete. Data in: $STAGE_DIR"
echo "STAGE_DIR=$STAGE_DIR" > "/tmp/stage_${JOB_ID}.env"

Conditional Statements for HPC

Resource Checking:

#!/bin/bash

# Check if running on login or compute node
if [[ -n "$SLURM_JOB_ID" ]] || [[ -n "$PBS_JOBID" ]]; then
    echo "Running as batch job"
    export IS_BATCH=true
else
    echo "Running interactively"
    export IS_BATCH=false
fi

# Check available memory
TOTAL_MEM=$(free -g | awk '/^Mem:/ {print $2}')
if [[ $TOTAL_MEM -lt 32 ]]; then
    echo "Warning: Low memory node ($TOTAL_MEM GB)"
elif [[ $TOTAL_MEM -lt 64 ]]; then
    echo "Memory: adequate ($TOTAL_MEM GB)"
else
    echo "Memory: high ($TOTAL_MEM GB)"
fi

# Check GPU availability
if command -v nvidia-smi &> /dev/null; then
    GPU_COUNT=$(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name --format=csv,noheader | wc -l)
    if [[ $GPU_COUNT -gt 0 ]]; then
        echo "GPUs available: $GPU_COUNT"
    else
        echo "No GPUs detected"
    fi
else
    echo "No GPU support"
fi

Job Type Detection:

#!/bin/bash

# Determine job type from parameters
case "${JOB_TYPE:-default}" in
    serial)
        echo "Running serial job"
        ./serial_program
        ;;
    mpi)
        echo "Running MPI job on $SLURM_NTASKS processes"
        mpirun -np "$SLURM_NTASKS" ./mpi_program
        ;;
    openmp)
        echo "Running OpenMP job with $OMP_NUM_THREADS threads"
        ./openmp_program
        ;;
    gpu)
        echo "Running GPU job"
        CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./gpu_program
        ;;
    *)
        echo "Unknown job type: $JOB_TYPE"
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --ntasks=1

#SBATCH --array=1-100

# Process files in parallel using array
INPUT_DIR="/data/inputs"
OUTPUT_DIR="/data/outputs/${SLURM_ARRAY_JOB_ID}"

mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"

# Get file for this array task
FILES=($INPUT_DIR/*.dat)
FILE="${FILES[$((SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID - 1))]}"

if [[ -f "$FILE" ]]; then
    BASENAME=$(basename "$FILE")
    echo "Processing: $BASENAME"
    
    # Process the file

    echo "Completed: $BASENAME"
else
    echo "No file for task $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID"
fi

Loop Over Nodes for Distributed Processing:

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --nodes=4
#SBATCH --ntasks=4
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1

# Get node list
NODES=$(scontrol show hostname "$SLURM_JOB_NODELIST")

# Run commands on each node
TASK_ID=0
for NODE in $NODES; do
    echo "Running on node: $NODE"
    
    # Launch task on specific node
    srun --nodes=1 --ntasks=1 --nodelist="$NODE" \
        ./node_task "$TASK_ID" &
    
    ((TASK_ID++))
done

wait
echo "All node tasks completed"

Functions for Reusable HPC Code

Function Library for HPC Scripts:

#!/bin/bash
# hpc_functions.sh - Reusable HPC functions

# Logging function
log_message() {
    local level="$1"
    local message="$2"
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] [$level] $message"
}

# Check job environment
check_job_environment() {
    if [[ -n "$SLURM_JOB_ID" ]]; then
        echo "SLURM"
        echo "JOB_ID=$SLURM_JOB_ID"
        echo "NODES=$SLURM_JOB_NODELIST"
    elif [[ -n "$PBS_JOBID" ]]; then
        echo "TORQUE"
        echo "JOB_ID=$PBS_JOBID"
        echo "NODES=$(cat $PBS_NODEFILE | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')"
    else
        echo "INTERACTIVE"
        echo "JOB_ID=$$"
        echo "NODES=$(hostname)"
    fi
}

# Wait for file with timeout
wait_for_file() {
    local file="$1"
    local timeout="${2:-300}"
    local elapsed=0
    
    while [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && [[ $elapsed -lt $timeout ]]; do
        sleep 5
        elapsed=$((elapsed + 5))
        echo "Waiting for $file ($elapsed/$timeout seconds)"
    done
    
    if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        return 1
    fi
}

# Get job statistics
get_job_stats() {
    local job_id="$1"
    
    if command -v sacct &> /dev/null; then
        sacct -j "$job_id" --format=JobID,Elapsed,State,ExitCode,MaxRSS,MaxVMSize --noheader
    elif command -v qstat &> /dev/null; then
        qstat -f "$job_id" | grep -E "Job_Owner|resources_used|job_state"
    else
        echo "No scheduler found"
    fi
}

# Load module with error handling
load_module() {
    local module_name="$1"
    
    if command -v module &> /dev/null; then
        module load "$module_name"
        if [[ $? -eq 0 ]]; then
            echo "Loaded module: $module_name"
        else
            echo "Failed to load module: $module_name"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        echo "Module system not available"
        return 1
    fi
}

export -f log_message check_job_environment wait_for_file get_job_stats load_module

Arrays for HPC Data Management

Managing Job Arrays:

#!/bin/bash

# Array of job IDs for dependency tracking
declare -a JOB_ARRAY

# Submit multiple jobs and track IDs
for i in {1..10}; do
    JOB_ID=$(sbatch --parsable "job_${i}.slurm")
    JOB_ARRAY+=("$JOB_ID")
    echo "Submitted: $JOB_ID"
done

# Convert array to comma-separated list
JOB_LIST=$(IFS=,; echo "${JOB_ARRAY[*]}")
echo "All jobs: $JOB_LIST"

# Submit dependent job
if [[ ${#JOB_ARRAY[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    sbatch --dependency=afterok:$JOB_LIST final_job.slurm
fi

Associative Arrays for Node Properties:

#!/bin/bash

declare -A NODE_PROPERTIES

# Get node information
while read -r node; do
    # Get CPU count
    CPUS=$(sinfo -n "$node" -o "%c" --noheader 2>/dev/null)
    # Get memory
    MEM=$(sinfo -n "$node" -o "%m" --noheader 2>/dev/null)
    # Get state
    STATE=$(sinfo -n "$node" -o "%t" --noheader 2>/dev/null)
    
    NODE_PROPERTIES["$node,cpus"]=$CPUS
    NODE_PROPERTIES["$node,mem"]=$MEM
    NODE_PROPERTIES["$node,state"]=$STATE
done <<< "$(sinfo -o "%n" --noheader | head -20)"

# Display node properties
for node in "${!NODE_PROPERTIES[@]}"; do
    echo "$node: ${NODE_PROPERTIES[$node]}"
done

Exit Codes and Error Handling in HPC

Job Failure Detection:

#!/bin/bash
# job_with_error_handling.sh

set -euo pipefail

# Trap errors
trap 'handle_error $? $LINENO' ERR

handle_error() {
    local exit_code="$1"
    local line_no="$2"
    
    echo "ERROR: Job failed at line $line_no with exit code $exit_code"
    echo "Job ID: ${SLURM_JOB_ID:-$PBS_JOBID}"
    
    # Send alert
    mail -s "HPC Job Failed: ${SLURM_JOB_NAME:-Unknown}" \
        "admin@hpc.et" << EOF
Job failed at $(date)
Exit code: $exit_code
Line: $line_no
Node: $(hostname)
EOF
    
    exit "$exit_code"
}

# Check critical prerequisites
check_prerequisites() {
    local missing=0
    
    for cmd in mpirun python3 gcc; do
        if ! command -v "$cmd" &> /dev/null; then
            echo "Missing: $cmd"
            missing=1
        fi
    done
    
    if [[ $missing -eq 1 ]]; then
        echo "Prerequisites not met"
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Main execution
main() {
    check_prerequisites
    
    echo "Starting job at $(date)"
    
    # Your actual work
    ./critical_application
    
    echo "Job completed at $(date)"
}

main "$@"

Job Wrapper with Retry Logic:

#!/bin/bash
# retry_wrapper.sh - Retry failed jobs

MAX_RETRIES=3
RETRY_DELAY=60

run_with_retry() {
    local cmd="$1"
    local attempt=1
    
    while [[ $attempt -le $MAX_RETRIES ]]; do
        echo "Attempt $attempt of $MAX_RETRIES"
        
        if eval "$cmd"; then
            echo "Command succeeded on attempt $attempt"
            return 0
        else
            echo "Command failed (attempt $attempt)"
            if [[ $attempt -lt $MAX_RETRIES ]]; then
                echo "Waiting $RETRY_DELAY seconds before retry..."
                sleep $RETRY_DELAY
            fi
        fi
        
        ((attempt++))
    done
    
    echo "Command failed after $MAX_RETRIES attempts"
    return 1
}

# Usage
run_with_retry "./my_application --input data.dat"

Text Processing for Log Analysis

Parsing Slurm Accounting Data:

#!/bin/bash
# parse_sacct.sh - Parse and analyze job accounting

# Get job data for last 7 days
sacct -S "now-7days" --format=JobID,JobName,User,State,Elapsed,ReqMem,MaxRSS,NodeList \
    --noheader -P > job_data.txt

# Analyze by user
echo "=== Jobs by User ==="
awk -F'|' '{print $3}' job_data.txt | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

# Analyze success rate
echo ""
echo "=== Job Success Rate ==="
TOTAL=$(wc -l < job_data.txt)
SUCCESS=$(grep -c "COMPLETED" job_data.txt)
echo "Total: $TOTAL"
echo "Success: $SUCCESS"
echo "Rate: $(echo "scale=2; $SUCCESS * 100 / $TOTAL" | bc)%"

# Analyze memory usage
echo ""
echo "=== Memory Usage Analysis ==="
awk -F'|' '
/COMPLETED/ {
    req = $6
    max = $7
    gsub(/[^0-9]/, "", req)
    gsub(/[^0-9]/, "", max)
    if (req > 0) {
        efficiency = (max / req) * 100
        printf "Job %s: %.1f%% memory efficiency\n", $2, efficiency
    }
}
' job_data.txt | head -20

Extract Node Utilization:

#!/bin/bash
# node_utilization.sh - Calculate node utilization

# Get job data with node lists
sacct -S "now-1day" --format=JobID,State,NodeList --noheader -P | \
    grep COMPLETED | \
    awk -F'|' '
    {
        split($3, nodes, ",")
        for (node in nodes) {
            node_count[nodes[node]]++
        }
    }
    END {
        for (node in node_count) {
            printf "%-20s %d jobs\n", node, node_count[node]
        }
    }' | sort -k2 -rn | head -20

Practical HPC Project - Weather Modeling

Complete Weather Model Workflow:

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=weather_ethiopia
#SBATCH --nodes=8
#SBATCH --ntasks=64
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=2
#SBATCH --mem=128G
#SBATCH --time=72:00:00
#SBATCH --partition=compute
#SBATCH --output=logs/weather_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=logs/weather_%j.err

# Weather modeling for Ethiopian Meteorology Institute
# Author: Bontu Megersa

set -euo pipefail

# Configuration
MODEL_DIR="/opt/models/wrf"
INPUT_DATA="/data/weather/$(date +%Y%m%d)"
OUTPUT_DIR="/results/weather/$(date +%Y%m%d)"
DOMAIN_FILE="ethiopia_domain.nl"
NML_FILE="namelist.input"

# Load environment
module purge
module load intel/2020
module load openmpi/4.0
module load netcdf/4.7
module load wrf/4.2

# Create output directory
mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"/{logs,plots,forecast}

log_message() {
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $1"
}

log_message "Starting WRF simulation for Ethiopian domain"

# Stage input data
log_message "Staging input data"
cp "$INPUT_DATA"/* "$TMPDIR/" || {
    log_message "ERROR: Failed to stage input data"
    exit 1
}

# Run WPS (Weather Preprocessing System)
log_message "Running WPS"
cd "$MODEL_DIR/WPS"
./geogrid.exe || exit 1
./ungrib.exe || exit 1
./metgrid.exe || exit 1

# Run WRF
log_message "Running WRF model"
cd "$MODEL_DIR/WRF/test/em_real"

# Update namelist for this run
sed -i "s/start_year = .*/start_year = $(date +%Y)/" "$NML_FILE"
sed -i "s/start_month = .*/start_month = $(date +%m)/" "$NML_FILE"
sed -i "s/start_day = .*/start_day = $(date +%d)/" "$NML_FILE"

# Run with MPI
mpirun -np 64 ./wrf.exe

# Process results
log_message "Processing forecast data"

# Extract temperature forecasts for major cities
CITIES="Addis_Ababa:9.03,38.74 Gondar:12.60,37.47 Jimma:7.67,36.83 Mekelle:13.50,39.47"

for city in $CITIES; do
    NAME=$(echo "$city" | cut -d: -f1)
    COORDS=$(echo "$city" | cut -d: -f2)
    LAT=$(echo "$COORDS" | cut -d, -f1)
    LON=$(echo "$COORDS" | cut -d, -f2)
    
    ncl "extract_point.ncl" "lat=$LAT" "lon=$LON" "city=\"$NAME\"" \
        "infile=\"wrfout_d01_*\""
    
    mv "${NAME}_forecast.txt" "$OUTPUT_DIR/forecast/"
done

# Generate forecast plots
python3 /opt/scripts/plot_forecast.py \
    --input wrfout_d01_* \
    --output "$OUTPUT_DIR/plots" \
    --variables temperature,precipitation,wind

# Create summary report
cat > "$OUTPUT_DIR/summary.txt" << EOF
Weather Forecast Summary
Date: $(date)
Domain: Ethiopia
Model: WRF 4.2
Resolution: 10km

Forecast available in:
- Plots: $OUTPUT_DIR/plots/
- Data: $OUTPUT_DIR/forecast/

Model run completed at $(date)
EOF

log_message "Weather simulation completed"

System Administration - Backup and Restore

HPC Backup Script:

#!/bin/bash
# backup_hpc.sh - Backup critical HPC data

BACKUP_DEST="/backup/hpc"
BACKUP_DATE=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BACKUP_DIR="$BACKUP_DEST/$BACKUP_DATE"
RETENTION_DAYS=30

# Directories to backup
BACKUP_PATHS=(
    "/home"
    "/project"
    "/opt/slurm/etc"
    "/opt/torque/server_priv"
    "/etc/slurm"
    "/etc/torque"
)

# Create backup directory
mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"

log() {
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $1"
}

log "Starting HPC backup to $BACKUP_DIR"

# Backup each directory
for path in "${BACKUP_PATHS[@]}"; do
    if [[ -d "$path" ]]; then
        BASENAME=$(basename "$path")
        BACKUP_FILE="$BACKUP_DIR/${BASENAME}_${BACKUP_DATE}.tar.gz"
        
        log "Backing up: $path"
        tar -czf "$BACKUP_FILE" "$path" 2>/dev/null
        
        if [[ $? -eq 0 ]]; then
            log "Success: $BASENAME"
        else
            log "ERROR: Failed to backup $BASENAME"
        fi
    else
        log "Warning: $path does not exist"
    fi
done

# Backup Slurm database
if command -v mysqldump &> /dev/null; then
    log "Backing up Slurm database"
    mysqldump slurm_acct_db > "$BACKUP_DIR/slurm_db_${BACKUP_DATE}.sql"
fi

# Backup Torque server state
if [[ -d "/var/spool/torque/server_priv" ]]; then
    log "Backing up Torque state"
    tar -czf "$BACKUP_DIR/torque_state_${BACKUP_DATE}.tar.gz" \
        /var/spool/torque/server_priv/jobs \
        /var/spool/torque/server_priv/nodes
fi

# Calculate backup size
BACKUP_SIZE=$(du -sh "$BACKUP_DIR" | cut -f1)
log "Backup size: $BACKUP_SIZE"

# Remove old backups
log "Removing backups older than $RETENTION_DAYS days"
find "$BACKUP_DEST" -type d -mtime +$RETENTION_DAYS -exec rm -rf {} \;

log "Backup completed successfully"

# Send report
mail -s "HPC Backup Report - $BACKUP_DATE" admin@hpc.et << EOF
Backup completed at $(date)
Location: $BACKUP_DIR
Size: $BACKUP_SIZE
Directories backed up: ${#BACKUP_PATHS[@]}
EOF

Best Practices for HPC Scripting

HPC-Specific Best Practices:

#!/bin/bash
# hpc_best_practices.sh - Template following best practices

# 1. Always use strict error handling
set -euo pipefail

# 2. Define all variables at top
readonly SCRIPT_NAME=$(basename "$0")
readonly SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
readonly LOG_FILE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/logs/${SLURM_JOB_ID:-$$}.log"

# 3. Use functions for reusable code
setup_environment() {
    # Load modules only when needed
    module purge
    module load gcc/10.2
    module load openmpi/4.1
    
    # Set temporary directories
    export TMPDIR="/scratch/${SLURM_JOB_ID:-$$}/tmp"
    mkdir -p "$TMPDIR"
}

cleanup() {
    # Clean up temporary files
    rm -rf "/scratch/${SLURM_JOB_ID:-$$}"
}

# 4. Use traps for cleanup
trap cleanup EXIT

# 5. Check for required resources
check_resources() {
    local required_mem_gb=32
    local available_mem_gb=$(free -g | awk '/^Mem:/ {print $7}')
    
    if [[ $available_mem_gb -lt $required_mem_gb ]]; then
        echo "Error: Insufficient memory" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
}

# 6. Log everything
log() {
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
}

# 7. Use version control for scripts
# 8. Test on small scale before full production
# 9. Document resource requirements
# 10. Use job arrays for parameter sweeps

Checklist for HPC Scripts: - [ ] Set set -euo pipefail - [ ] Define walltime limit - [ ] Request appropriate memory - [ ] Set email notifications - [ ] Use scratch space for temporary files - [ ] Clean up temporary files - [ ] Log job steps and errors - [ ] Test with small input first - [ ] Document module dependencies - [ ] Use absolute paths

Common HPC Script Patterns

Pattern 1: Master-Worker:

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --nodes=5
#SBATCH --ntasks=5

# Master node (rank 0) distributes work
if [[ $SLURM_PROCID -eq 0 ]]; then
    for worker in {1..4}; do
        srun --ntasks=1 --nodes=1 ./worker_task "$worker" &
    done
    wait
else
    # Worker nodes process
    ./worker_process "$SLURM_PROCID"
fi

Pattern 2: Pipeline:

#!/bin/bash

# Stage 1: Preprocess
sbatch --parsable preprocess.slurm > job1.id

# Stage 2: Compute (depends on preprocess)
JOB1=$(cat job1.id)
sbatch --parsable --dependency=afterok:$JOB1 compute.slurm > job2.id

# Stage 3: Postprocess (depends on compute)
JOB2=$(cat job2.id)
sbatch --dependency=afterok:$JOB2 postprocess.slurm

Pattern 3: Checkpoint-Restart:

#!/bin/bash

CHECKPOINT_FILE="checkpoint.chk"
MAX_TIME=3600

if [[ -f "$CHECKPOINT_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "Restarting from checkpoint"
    ./app --restore "$CHECKPOINT_FILE"
else
    echo "Starting fresh"
    ./app --checkpoint-interval 300 --checkpoint-file "$CHECKPOINT_FILE"
fi

Troubleshooting and Debugging

Common HPC Job Failures:

Symptom Likely Cause Solution
Out of memory Requested memory too low Increase #SBATCH --mem
Timeout Walltime too short Increase --time
Node allocation failed Insufficient resources Check queue with sinfo
Module not found Module path issue Check module avail
Permission denied File ownership issue Check ls -la
MPI errors Network or version mismatch Test with mpirun --version

Debug Script:

#!/bin/bash
# debug_hpc_job.sh - Debug failing HPC job

echo "=== Debug Information ==="
echo "Job ID: ${SLURM_JOB_ID:-$PBS_JOBID}"
echo "Hostname: $(hostname)"
echo "Date: $(date)"
echo "User: $(whoami)"
echo ""

echo "=== Environment ==="
env | sort | head -20
echo ""

echo "=== Modules ==="
module list 2>/dev/null || echo "No module system"
echo ""

echo "=== Disk Space ==="
df -h /home /scratch /project
echo ""

echo "=== Memory ==="
free -g
echo ""

echo "=== Process Limits ==="
ulimit -a
echo ""

echo "=== Job Details ==="
if command -v scontrol &> /dev/null; then
    scontrol show job "$SLURM_JOB_ID"
elif command -v qstat &> /dev/null; then
    qstat -f "$PBS_JOBID"
fi
